The thing is it is possible to get a mortgage without a credit score, but it requires quite a lot of shopping around. You need to find a bank/CU willing to do "manual underwriting", which is the way creditworthiness was determined prior to credit bureaus. This process actually happens in all mortgages eventually, but without a credit score, you are asking lenders to put in all that legwork at the very start of the process, when it is possible that you're just shopping rates and will bail on them in a week. This makes most large firms refuse to do it, so your best bet is a smaller credit union in your town.

Your rate will be higher than their average and you will be treated as a risky loan. However, you will build credit after a few years of payments and may be able to refi a better deal. Interestingly, since you probably don't carry any other debt your debt to income ratio will be low even with a large mortgage payment, so they may actually authorize a bigger loan than you expect.

You will need a couple years of tax records, proof of income/employment, proof of liquid assets (to show you have a down payment), several pay stubs, records of regular on time payments for rent/utilities/cars/anything. Be prepared to show where any non-employment deposits of over $300 came from.

Also, if you have a shitty score (rather than having no score / unscoreable) the bank will have to use that, and may not go through the manual process at all.
